conventions.convention: The kernel has fixed order (r,r), is measurable on the finite product sigma-algebra, and is symmetric separately within each block. The parameter is its integral under P^r × Q^r; antisymmetry and a zero parameter are additional hypotheses.

The U-statistic averages over unordered index subsets; selected observations are listed in increasing index order. First projections are centered square-integrable equivalence classes represented by measurable section integrals.

Standard-error studentization is S = U/[r sqrt(estimated variance X/m + estimated variance Y/n)], with S = 0 when the denominator is zero. S itself, without an additional sqrt(m), is the normal pivot.
Both variance estimates are recomputed on each permutation. Estimates may depend on both groups; separate-group dependence is an additional condition.
The IID comparison mixture uses the exact row weight p_N = m/N. The contiguity direction used is binomial-small events imply hypergeometric-small events; no rate for p_N − p is required.

General joint variance estimates require conditional permutation consistency explicitly. IID triangular-mixture consistency is sufficient through the transfer lemma only for estimates depending on their own group alone.

Finite-group ranks count group elements with multiplicity. Inclusive upper ranks are superuniform; independent uniform randomization within the equality block gives uniform p-values under an invariant law.

The weak-null permutation theorem assumes AC, block antisymmetry, positive finite second moments under every independent P/Q assignment, and positive pooled first-projection variance. It does not assume assignment-wise centering.
The Wilcoxon kernel is 1{y > x} − 1{y < x}, with zero on ties. Its null is P(X < Y) + P(X = Y)/2 = 1/2, rather than equality of means or medians.

load_bearing.statement: For fixed r, m+n=N, m/N→p∈(0,1), a block-symmetric and block-antisymmetric kernel with finite second moments under every independent P/Q assignment admits the stated exact-triangular-mixture coupling with sqrt(m)(U(Z^π)−U(bar Z^{ππ₀}))→0 in L². Neither the weak null nor assignment-wise kernel centering is needed.

Assume AC. For IID mean-zero real rows with variances tending to σ²>0 and uniformly integrable squares, and an independent uniform size-m_N subset with m_N/N→p∈(0,1), the displayed finite-population-variance-normalized centered subset sum, set to zero when S_N²=0, has conditional CDF converging uniformly in probability to Φ.

Under AC, independent IID P and Q samples, m/N→p∈(0,1), θ(P,Q;h)=0, fixed block-symmetric and block-antisymmetric h, positive finite second moments for every independent P/Q assignment, and σ_p²>0, the conditional permutation CDF of sqrt(m)U converges uniformly in probability to the CDF of N(0,r²σ_p²/(1−p)).

Under its AC, weak-null, mixed-moment and positive direct/pooled projection hypotheses, direct consistency of the nonnegative variance estimates and their stated conditional permutation consistency imply both S→N(0,1) in distribution under true sampling and uniform conditional permutation CDF convergence to Φ. Own-group IID triangular-mixture consistency is a sufficient condition for permutation consistency.

For fixed r, proportionally growing independent IID groups with row laws P_N,Q_N, and a uniform finite bound on the kernel second moment over every independent P_N/Q_N assignment, E_N[R²]=O(N⁻²) and sqrt(N)R→0 in L².

Assume AC. A measurable statistic of one group of size k_N∈{m_N,n_N}, consistent for a deterministic target c_N on IID samples from (m_N/N)P+(n_N/N)Q, remains consistent for c_N on the corresponding uniformly permuted pooled group.

For a uniform permutation π of N≥1 elements and any real function f, Var(f(π)) ≤ (1/2)Σ_k (N−k+1)⁻¹Σ_{l=k}^N E[(f(π)−f(π(k,l)))²]. In particular, a common second-moment bound b on transposition differences gives Var(f(π))≤Nb/2.

concerns.concern: The Statement claims E_P[g_X²]≤E[h²] and E_Q[g_Y²]≤E[h²]. Step 2.1 establishes these bounds for the uncentered section functions f_X,f_Y, while step 3.1 concludes centering and square-integrability without explicitly deriving the displayed centered bounds. The missing line is E[(f−θ)²]=E[f²]−θ²≤E[f²], using Ef=θ. This closes immediately and does not undermine the claim.
